Subject: Private on‑prem deep dive: hardware, offline upgrades, and site survey

Hi Alice — thanks again for the time today. Quick recap and next steps from our side so we have alignment: 

Recap (high level)
- Deployment mode: ThermoGen prefers Private (on‑prem, air‑gapped) for IP/data residency.
- Hardware baseline discussed: current estate is HPE Gen10 with options to add GPU nodes (you mentioned interest in A100/RTX 6000 class). Exact SKU TBD.
- Operational constraints: maintenance windows must be scheduled (no more than quarterly), upgrades often must be performed offline, and patch approvals will go through your security team.
- Requirements we still need: network/rack diagrams, current hardware SKUs, spare parts / spares policy, and a finalized SOC2 questionnaire.

Attachments: I attached a site_survey_template.pdf to capture environment details and network constraints.

Proposed next steps
1) Alice — please send the filled site survey and the SOC2 scoping answers (if possible) by EOD Wed (7/14).
2) Karthik — please draft a rough SOW/price band for a 3‑node and 8‑node private deployment (include travel, on‑site commissioning, and 12‑month support). Target: sharing by Fri 7/16.
3) Soojin — validate the likely compatibility with HPE config and list any immediate red flags (power, NICs, special kernel/driver needs).
4) We'll propose two dates for an on‑site survey next week once we have the site survey back.

If that sounds good I’ll ping you with proposed windows. Thanks again — folks copied for visibility.

— Ben Carter
Senior Account Executive
Redwood Inference

Ben— thanks for the summary. Agree on the approach; a few clarifications below and I attached our preliminary SOC2 scoping answers.

Quick answers
- Hardware: we currently run HPE ProLiant DL380 Gen10 servers. For ML inference workloads we are evaluating adding nodes populated with 4x A100 40GB (NVLink not required initially). Estimate total GPU requirement: 16 GPUs to start (8‑node config with 2x GPUs each OR 4 nodes with 4x).
- Network: isolated management VLAN for the infra, no outbound internet from the cluster except controlled jump host. All upgrades must happen via air‑gap media or an approved jump host under our control.
- Patch cadence: major upgrades quarterly, security hotfixes on an as‑needed basis after our internal review.
- Spare policy: we have a pool of critical spares (PSUs, NICs) but not GPU spares — lead time for GPUs is currently 6‑8 weeks.

We’ve attached ThermoGen_SOC2_Q&A.xlsx with initial answers and marked items we expect Redwood to supply as part of implementation. I’ll try to complete the site survey by EOD Wednesday but may need until Thu morning — hope that’s OK.

Best,
Alice Park
Head of Infrastructure Operations, ThermoGen

Folks — forwarding Alice’s response. Highlights for our deliverables: 

Action items (internal owners)
- Soojin: confirm driver/kernel/OS compatibility for HPE DL380 Gen10 + 4x A100 40GB. Call out any special NIC/firmware constraints and whether NVLink or DGX‑style topologies are required for performance targets. Also outline an offline upgrade process that respects their no‑internet rule (we’ll need a verified media signing approach or jump host plan). Target: initial findings by EOD Thu 7/15.
- Karthik: sketch two SOW options (3‑node starter and 8‑node scale) with rough cost bands, one‑time commissioning fees, and 12‑month support. Include travel estimate for 2x engineers for 3 days each. Target: draft by Fri 7/16.
- Ben: I’ll propose on‑site survey windows for next week once Alice confirms site survey date. Also will prepare a short acceptance test checklist (smoke tests + model latency checks) to share with them.

Notes: GPU lead times are long — if they need immediate capacity we should propose a hybrid ramp (start with hosted/dedicated burst until hardware arrives). Might be a good upsell.

— Ben

Thanks Ben/Alice — quick read here, initial technical notes below. Will put a short checklist together and follow with a deeper compatibility note by Thu.

Initial technical notes
- HPE DL380 Gen10: supported, but confirm BIOS and iLO versions. For 4x A100 40GB we recommend verifying power headroom (PDU circuits) and that chassis airflow meets GPU thermal profiles.
- Drivers/OS: we prefer Ubuntu 22.04 LTS with NVIDIA driver 535+ and CUDA 12+ for best compatibility. If ThermoGen has a hardened OS baseline, we’ll need the image to validate kernel module signing.
- Air‑gap upgrades: propose a signed tarball approach + checksum + ephemeral jump host model. We’ll draft an offline upgrade playbook (includes presigned artifacts and a local package repo workflow).
- Acceptance tests: will include model latency (p95), KV‑cache warmup behavior, and a rolling upgrade sanity test that validates no token loss and a fallback to a lower‑capacity model if upgrade hangs.

Requests
- Alice: can you share rack elevations and current PDU circuit list prior to the on‑site survey? Also helpful: OS image fingerprint and any vendor‑managed HSM/KMS info.

I’ll target the compatibility note + checklist by Thu 2027‑07‑15 COB.

— Soojin Lee
Solutions Architect, Redwood Inference

1) Site survey: we have two windows open next Wed 7/21 and Thu 7/22 (09:00–13:00 local). Please confirm which works for your ops team and if we should include facility security/SCADA contacts.

2) Prework: if you can share rack elevations and the PDU list (So they can be uploaded to the site_survey_template), that will accelerate the compatibility checks Soojin will run. If site survey slips to Thu morning that’s fine.

3) Hybrid ramp option: given GPU lead times, recommend we include a brief plan that starts with Redwood Hosted / Dedicated capacity for burst traffic during procurement. We’ll include this in the SOW options Karthik drafts.

- Alice: site survey + rack/PDU list (target Thu 7/15 morning if possible).

If all good I’ll lock the survey window once you confirm. Thanks — looking forward to moving to an on‑site assessment.
